skill.name: baoyu-url-to-markdown
skill.description: Fetch a URL in Chrome, extract the rendered page, and save clean Markdown with metadata.
skill.summary: Convert rendered web pages into local Markdown files through Chrome CDP.
skill.author: jimliu

security_audit.summary: This skill launches Chrome, opens a loopback CDP connection, fetches user-provided pages, and writes captured content to disk. Most static hits on template literals, Markdown backticks, user-agent strings, and benign path checks are false positives. Remaining concerns are external process execution, arbitrary URL browsing, output-file writes, and hidden EXTEND.md configuration instructions.

remediation.suggestion: Resolve requested output paths under an approved root, reject path traversal, and require confirmation before overwriting files.
Restrict captures to http and https URLs, and warn before visiting localhost, private IP ranges, or file-like schemes.
Validate URL_CHROME_PATH, document that Chrome is launched locally, and avoid accepting untrusted executable paths.
Parse preferences as strict data only, ignore executable instructions, and ask before reading user-home configuration.
Warn users before wait-mode capture and avoid saving pages that contain secrets, account data, or regulated information.

content.value_statement: Web pages are hard to reuse when content depends on JavaScript or login state. This skill opens the page in Chrome and saves rendered content as Markdown.
actual_capabilities: Opens a user-provided URL in Chrome through the Chrome DevTools Protocol.
Supports automatic capture after page load and network idle.
Supports wait mode for pages that need manual login or interaction.
Converts common HTML elements into Markdown with YAML metadata.
Saves output to an automatic domain path or a requested file path.
limitations: Requires Chrome or a compatible browser installed on the local machine.
Runs local scripts and launches a browser process.
Uses simple conversion rules, so complex layouts may lose structure.
Does not enforce URL host restrictions or output path restrictions.

use_cases.title: Archive Research Articles
use_cases.description: Save public articles as Markdown for notes, citations, and offline review.

use_cases.title: Build Documentation Notes
use_cases.description: Capture rendered product pages or blog posts into a local knowledge base.

use_cases.title: Capture Rendered App Pages
use_cases.description: Save pages that need JavaScript rendering, lazy loading, or manual readiness checks.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to convert https://example.com/article into Markdown. Save it in the default output folder.

prompt_templates.title: Capture After Login
prompt_templates.scenario: Wait mode for manual page readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the URL in wait mode. Pause until I confirm the page is ready, then save the Markdown output.

prompt_templates.title: Save to a Named File
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the URL to Markdown and write it to docs/reference/page-notes.md. Confirm before overwriting an existing file.

prompt_templates.title: Archive Several Pages
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these URLs one at a time, use wait mode when needed, and summarize each saved file path and title.

output_examples.output: A Markdown file with metadata, title, headings, links, images, lists, and cleaned article text.
A local Markdown capture taken after user confirmation, with source URL and capture time in metadata.

output_examples.input: Page with an existing saved title
output_examples.output: A new Markdown file with a timestamp added to avoid overwriting the earlier capture.

best_practices: Review URLs before capture, especially when they come from untrusted input.
Use wait mode only after confirming the page is ready and safe to persist.
Save within the project or default data directory unless an absolute path is necessary.
anti_patterns: Do not capture private pages that contain secrets, tokens, or customer data.
Do not use the output path option to overwrite source files or configuration files.
Do not treat converted Markdown as sanitized HTML or security-reviewed content.

faq.question: Does this skill require Chrome?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs Chrome, Chromium, or Edge available on the local machine.

faq.question: Can it capture pages after login?
faq.answer: Yes. Wait mode lets the user prepare the page before capture. Use care with private account content.

faq.question: Where are files saved?
faq.answer: By default, files are saved under a url-to-markdown folder by domain and title slug.

faq.question: Does it make network requests?
faq.answer: Yes. Chrome loads the requested page, and the script talks to a local Chrome debugging endpoint.

faq.question: Does it sanitize unsafe web content?
faq.answer: No. It removes common page clutter, but the Markdown should not be treated as sanitized content.

faq.question: Can I choose the output path?
faq.answer: Yes. The output option can write to a chosen path, so confirm paths before running it.
